-- EP-488 v50 / G4: Degree-3 vertices are nonadjacent
-- Claim: If both a and b have degree 3 in B_n, they are not adjacent in the
-- n-LCM graph.
--
-- Proof idea: Any neighbor of a degree-3 vertex a is in {3a/2, 4a/3, 5a/3, 5a/4},
-- all strictly greater than 3q/5 (need to verify each). But every degree-3
-- vertex is strictly less than 3q/5. So a degree-3 vertex cannot be a neighbor
-- of another degree-3 vertex.
--
-- Simplified target: show that if a < 3q/5 and b is a potential neighbor of a
-- (meaning b is one of 3a/2, 4a/3, 5a/3, 5a/4 as integers), then b ≥ 3q/5.
-- Hence b cannot itself be a degree-3 vertex.

import Mathlib.Tactic

/-- If a > q/2, then 3a/2 ≥ 3q/4 > 3q/5. -/
theorem neighbor_3a_2_exceeds_3q_5
    {q a : ℕ}
    (hq : 0 < q)
    (ha : q / 2 < a)
    (hdiv : 2 ∣ a) :
    5 * (3 * a / 2) ≥ 3 * q := by
  sorry

/-- If a > q/2, then 4a/3 > 2q/3 > 3q/5. -/
theorem neighbor_4a_3_exceeds_3q_5
    {q a : ℕ}
    (hq : 0 < q)
    (ha : q / 2 < a)
    (hdiv : 3 ∣ a) :
    5 * (4 * a / 3) ≥ 3 * q := by
  sorry
